title: Inheritance and custom properties
summary: Let children inherit styles from parents, and store reusable values in CSS variables.

quiz.q: You set `body { color: navy; }`. What colour is a paragraph with no colour rule of its own?
quiz.explain: `color` is an inherited property, so children use the parent's value unless a rule says otherwise.

quiz.q: Which of these is **not** inherited by default?
quiz.explain: Text properties tend to inherit. Box properties such as `border`, `margin` and `padding` do not, otherwise every child would get its parent's border.

quiz.q: Complete the line that uses the variable.
quiz.explain: Define the variable with two dashes, for example `--brand: #0057b8;`, and read it with `var(--brand)`.

quiz.q: Why is `:root` a good place to define variables?
options: It matches the html element, so every element can use them
quiz.explain: `:root` is the top element. Custom properties are inherited, so everything on the page can read variables defined there.

exercise.task:
Use inheritance and variables. Work in `index.html`.

- In `:root` define `--brand: #0057b8;` and `--space: 16px;`.
- Give `body` a `color` of `darkslategray`. Do **not** style `p` directly: it should inherit.
- Make `h1` use `color: var(--brand)`.
- Make `.btn` use `background-color: var(--brand)` and `padding: var(--space)`.
hints: Custom property names start with two dashes. Define them inside `:root { ... }`.
Set `color` on body only. For the others, write `var(--name)` in place of a value.

checks.name: No rule targets p directly
checks.hint: Remove any p rule. The paragraph should get its colour from body by inheritance.

checks.name: The paragraph inherits darkslategray from body
checks.hint: Add body { color: darkslategray; } and do not add a rule for p.

checks.name: The h1 uses the brand colour through var()
The h1 is the brand colour
checks.hint: Make sure --brand is #0057b8 and the h1 uses it.
